question_text: A hockey puck slides on a frictionless ice surface at a constant velocity of 5 m/s. What net horizontal force is required to keep it moving at this constant speed?
correct_answer_and_steps: Net force required is 0 N. According to Newton's First Law of Motion, an object in motion continues to move at constant velocity unless acted upon by an external net unbalanced force. Frictionless surface means no force is needed to sustain motion.

evidence_details: Conflates force with momentum or constant velocity.

topic_concept: Free Fall & Acceleration due to Gravity
question_text: A heavy 10 kg iron ball and a light 1 kg wooden ball are dropped simultaneously from the same height in an evacuated vacuum chamber. Which ball hits the ground first?
correct_answer_and_steps: Both hit the ground at the exact same instant. Acceleration due to gravity g = G*M_earth / R^2 is independent of the falling object's mass m. While gravitational force is greater on the heavier object (F = mg), its inertial resistance to acceleration is proportionally greater by the exact same factor (a = F/m = g).
student_response: My answer is: Both hit at the exact same time because acceleration due to gravity g is independent of the mass of the falling body in vacuum..
evidence_details: Correct mass-independent free fall principle.

topic_concept: Cartesian Sign Convention in Mirror Formula
question_text: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Calculate image distance v using Cartesian signs.
correct_answer_and_steps: u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm. 1/v = 1/(-15) - 1/(-20) = -1/60 => v = -60 cm. Real and inverted image formed in front of mirror.

evidence_details: Substituted positive scalar distances.

topic_concept: Force on Charges and Current in Magnetic Field
question_text: An electron moves horizontally from West to East into a uniform magnetic field directed vertically downwards. Find force direction.
correct_answer_and_steps: Electron moves West to East, so current I is East to West. B is Down. By Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Forefinger (Field) = Down, Center (Current) = West => Thumb (Force) points South. For stationary proton, v = 0 so F = 0 N.
student_response: According to my working, Force points North because I used current in direction of electron motion (West to East).
misconception_label: MISC-MAG-005: Directional Hand Rule Inversion Fallacy
evidence_details: Failed to invert current for negative charge.
diagram_description: Magnetic field B directed downwards. Electron travels West to East. Conventional current points East to West. Force points South.
